quests.question: My aunt waters the tomato plants every evening.
quests.sentence: My aunt waters the tomato plants every evening.
quests.hint: Find the word right before the verb waters. Is that person doing the watering, or having it done to them?
quests.explanation: My aunt is the doer here: she performs the action waters directly on the tomato plants, which are the receiver. That doer-before-the-verb pattern is the clearest sign of active voice. Turned around, the same idea becomes passive: The tomato plants are watered every evening by my aunt.
quests.activeVoice: My aunt waters the tomato plants every evening.
quests.passiveVoice: The tomato plants are watered every evening by my aunt.

quests.question: The tomato plants are watered every evening by my aunt.
quests.sentence: The tomato plants are watered every evening by my aunt.
quests.hint: The subject, the tomato plants, cannot water anything. Ask what is actually happening to it.
quests.explanation: Here the tomato plants (the receiver) sit in subject position even though they don't perform the action - my aunt does. That's the heart of passive voice: the receiver of an action becomes the grammatical subject, with are watered marking the passive verb form. The same fact stated actively is: My aunt waters the tomato plants every evening.
quests.activeVoice: My aunt waters the tomato plants every evening.
quests.passiveVoice: The tomato plants are watered every evening by my aunt.

quests.question: Fresh bread is sold at the corner bakery.
quests.sentence: Fresh bread is sold at the corner bakery.
quests.hint: There's no named baker here. Ask instead: does the bread do the selling, or does something happen to it?
quests.explanation: Fresh bread cannot sell itself, so even without a named agent, this is still passive: the bread receives the action, marked by is sold. Passive sentences often drop the doer entirely when it's obvious or unimportant. A natural active version would need to supply a doer: The bakery sells fresh bread at the corner shop.
quests.activeVoice: The bakery sells fresh bread at the corner shop.
quests.passiveVoice: Fresh bread is sold at the corner bakery.

quests.question: This gym is open to members every day of the week.
quests.sentence: This gym is open to members every day of the week.
quests.hint: Check the verb carefully - is open here isn't a passive verb form at all. Ask whether anything is actually being done to the gym.
quests.explanation: This sentence only looks passive because it has is in it, but open is an adjective describing the gym's state, not a past participle showing an action done to it. No one is 'opening' the gym in this sentence - it simply describes a fact, so it counts as active in structure. Compare this with a true passive: The gym is opened by staff at six every morning.
quests.activeVoice: This gym is open to members every day of the week.
quests.passiveVoice: The gym is opened by staff at six every morning.

quests.question: New uniforms are issued to the team at the start of each season.
quests.sentence: New uniforms are issued to the team at the start of each season.
quests.hint: Ask whether the uniforms hand themselves out, or whether someone must be doing the issuing.
quests.explanation: The uniforms (receiver) are issued - someone else, left unnamed, must be doing the issuing. This is passive because the grammatical subject undergoes the action rather than performing it. Supplying a doer gives the active version: The club issues new uniforms to the team at the start of each season.
quests.activeVoice: The club issues new uniforms to the team at the start of each season.
quests.passiveVoice: New uniforms are issued to the team at the start of each season.

quests.question: Local farmers grow most of the vegetables sold in this market.
quests.sentence: Local farmers grow most of the vegetables sold in this market.
quests.hint: Two verbs appear here. Focus on the main one, grow, and find who is doing that growing.
quests.explanation: Local farmers is the doer of grow, so the main clause is active, even though sold later in the sentence describes the vegetables passively. Whenever a sentence contains more than one verb, decide voice clause by clause rather than judging the whole sentence at a glance. The main idea flipped to passive would read: Most of the vegetables sold in this market are grown by local farmers.
quests.activeVoice: Local farmers grow most of the vegetables sold in this market.
quests.passiveVoice: Most of the vegetables sold in this market are grown by local farmers.

quests.question: My uncle fixed the leaking faucet in ten minutes.
quests.sentence: My uncle fixed the leaking faucet in ten minutes.
quests.hint: Find who performed the action fixed. That person belongs right before the verb in active voice.
quests.explanation: My uncle is the doer of fixed, acting directly on the faucet, so this sentence is active. Notice the pattern doer + past-tense verb + receiver. The same event told from the faucet's point of view becomes passive: The leaking faucet was fixed in ten minutes by my uncle.
quests.activeVoice: My uncle fixed the leaking faucet in ten minutes.
quests.passiveVoice: The leaking faucet was fixed in ten minutes by my uncle.

quests.question: The window was cracked by a falling branch during the storm.
quests.sentence: The window was cracked by a falling branch during the storm.
quests.hint: Look for was plus a past-tense verb form that describes something happening to the window, not something the window did.
quests.explanation: The window (receiver) was cracked - it didn't crack anything itself. Was cracked is the passive form: was + past participle. The agent, a falling branch, is named after by, but even without that phrase the sentence would still be passive. Active version: A falling branch cracked the window during the storm.
quests.activeVoice: A falling branch cracked the window during the storm.
quests.passiveVoice: The window was cracked by a falling branch during the storm.

quests.question: Someone left a package outside my apartment door.
quests.sentence: Someone left a package outside my apartment door.
quests.hint: Even though we don't know who someone is, check whether they perform the action or receive it.
quests.explanation: Someone is a vague subject, but it still performs the action left, making this active voice - an unknown doer doesn't change the structure. Passive voice hides the doer differently, by removing the subject slot altogether: A package was left outside my apartment door.
quests.activeVoice: Someone left a package outside my apartment door.
quests.passiveVoice: A package was left outside my apartment door.

quests.question: The soup was seasoned with too much salt last night.
quests.sentence: The soup was seasoned with too much salt last night.
quests.hint: Ask whether the soup did the seasoning, or whether it happened to the soup.
quests.explanation: The soup (receiver) was seasoned - it cannot season itself, so this is passive even though no cook is named. Passive sentences frequently drop the doer when the sentence is more about the result than about who caused it. Naming a doer gives: The cook seasoned the soup with too much salt last night.
quests.activeVoice: The cook seasoned the soup with too much salt last night.
quests.passiveVoice: The soup was seasoned with too much salt last night.

quests.question: The store refunded my money without asking any questions.
quests.sentence: The store refunded my money without asking any questions.
quests.hint: Find who carried out the action refunded - it sits right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The store is the doer, performing refunded directly on my money, so this is active voice, not passive. Don't be misled by the word store sounding like a place rather than a person - grammatically it still acts as the subject doing the action. In passive form: My money was refunded without any questions being asked.
quests.activeVoice: The store refunded my money without asking any questions.
quests.passiveVoice: My money was refunded without any questions being asked.

quests.question: Two flights were cancelled because of the heavy fog.
quests.sentence: Two flights were cancelled because of the heavy fog.
quests.hint: Flights can't cancel themselves. Look for were plus the past participle that shows something being done to them.
quests.explanation: Two flights (receiver) were cancelled - the fog caused it, but the fog isn't grammatically named as an agent here. Were cancelled is the passive pattern for a plural subject. If we wanted to name a cause as agent, it would read: Heavy fog caused two flights to be cancelled - but the simplest active match is: The airline cancelled two flights because of the heavy fog.
quests.activeVoice: The airline cancelled two flights because of the heavy fog.
quests.passiveVoice: Two flights were cancelled because of the heavy fog.

quests.question: Complaints about noise are handled by the building manager.
quests.sentence: Complaints about noise are handled by the building manager.
quests.hint: Complaints cannot handle themselves. Look for are plus a past participle, then check if a doer is named after by.
quests.explanation: Complaints (receiver) are handled - the building manager is the true doer, but is named only after by, in the agent position rather than the subject position. This is the classic passive pattern: receiver-as-subject + be + past participle + by-agent. Active form: The building manager handles complaints about noise.
quests.activeVoice: The building manager handles complaints about noise.
quests.passiveVoice: Complaints about noise are handled by the building manager.

quests.question: Our barista remembers every regular customer's order by heart.
quests.sentence: Our barista remembers every regular customer's order by heart.
quests.hint: Who is doing the remembering? Find that word right before the verb.
quests.explanation: Our barista performs the action remembers directly on every regular customer's order, so this is active voice - remembers is never used in a passive form since it isn't the kind of verb typically flipped that way with a direct object like this. Passive version, if needed for emphasis: Every regular customer's order is remembered by our barista.
quests.activeVoice: Our barista remembers every regular customer's order by heart.
quests.passiveVoice: Every regular customer's order is remembered by our barista.

quests.question: The recycling gets collected on Tuesday mornings.
quests.sentence: The recycling gets collected on Tuesday mornings.
quests.hint: Notice the pattern gets + past participle. This is another way English forms the passive besides be.
quests.explanation: Gets collected is an informal passive pattern using get instead of be - the recycling (receiver) doesn't collect itself. Get-passives are common in everyday speech, especially for things that happen to someone or something. In more formal active language: The city collects the recycling on Tuesday mornings.
quests.activeVoice: The city collects the recycling on Tuesday mornings.
quests.passiveVoice: The recycling gets collected on Tuesday mornings.

quests.question: Volunteers rebuilt the playground after the flood.
quests.sentence: Volunteers rebuilt the playground after the flood.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before the past-tense verb rebuilt.
quests.explanation: Volunteers is the doer, performing rebuilt directly on the playground, which makes this active voice. Past-tense active verbs like rebuilt need no auxiliary at all, unlike their passive counterparts. Passive version: The playground was rebuilt by volunteers after the flood.
quests.activeVoice: Volunteers rebuilt the playground after the flood.
quests.passiveVoice: The playground was rebuilt by volunteers after the flood.

quests.question: The border was closed for nearly six months last year.
quests.sentence: The border was closed for nearly six months last year.
quests.hint: A border cannot close itself in this sense. Look for was plus a past participle describing what happened to it.
quests.explanation: The border (receiver) was closed - no specific authority is named as the agent, which is common when the exact decision-maker isn't the point of the sentence. This still counts as passive because the subject undergoes rather than performs the action. If we added a doer: Government officials closed the border for nearly six months last year.
quests.activeVoice: Government officials closed the border for nearly six months last year.
quests.passiveVoice: The border was closed for nearly six months last year.

quests.question: We finally reached the summit just before sunset.

quests.explanation: We is the doer here, performing reached directly on the summit, so this sentence is active. Notice that intransitive-feeling verbs like reach still take an object (the summit) and can be flipped to passive when needed: The summit was finally reached just before sunset.
quests.activeVoice: We finally reached the summit just before sunset.
quests.passiveVoice: The summit was finally reached just before sunset.

quests.explanation: Final exam scores (receiver) are posted - the school or teacher is the implied doer, but it's left out entirely, which passive voice easily allows. This kind of agentless passive is common when the process matters more than the person behind it. Active form: The school posts final exam scores within a week of the test date.
quests.activeVoice: The school posts final exam scores within a week of the test date.
